title: The Geometry of Dissipative Complexity: A Levi-Type Decomposition Theorem for Markovian Quantum Dynamics via Lie Wedges and Invariant Cones
abstract: Lie algebras describe how control Hamiltonians combine in closed quantum systems. In open Markovian systems, however, dissipation introduces irreversible directions that the Lie algebra alone does not retain. A dynamical Lie wedge preserves this information as a convex cone of locally admissible generators. The classical Levi decomposition separates a finite-dimensional Lie algebra into semisimple and solvable parts. In this work, we prove a corresponding decomposition and reconstruction theorem for dynamical Lie wedges.   The theorem decomposes the wedge into semisimple and solvable data, records how these components are coupled, and provides a converse reconstruction of the wedge. The framework yields four structural types of the generated algebra. We further prove that the total dissipation strength of every admissible generator depends only on its coordinate in the solvable radical. In particular, if the generated Lie algebra is semisimple, every admissible generator is Hamiltonian. Together, these results extend Lie-algebraic structural methods to irreversible Markovian control and clarify how dissipation is encoded in the generator geometry.
summary: This paper extends classical Lie algebra theory to open quantum systems by introducing the 'Dynamical Lie Wedge' to capture irreversible dissipation. It proves a Levi-Type Decomposition Theorem for this wedge, classifying the system's structure based on its semisimple and solvable components. This provides a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing quantum control in dissipative environments.
main_problem: To develop a structural classification framework for open quantum systems undergoing Markovian dynamics by extending the classical Levi decomposition from Lie algebras to the geometry of dissipative generators.
main_result: The authors prove a Levi-Type Decomposition Theorem for dynamical Lie wedges, decomposing the structure into semisimple and solvable components and providing a converse reconstruction.
method: The methodology combines Lie algebra theory (Levi decomposition) with convex geometry, utilizing the concept of the Dynamical Lie Wedge (a convex cone) to account for irreversible dissipation.
model_or_system: The focus is on open Markovian quantum systems whose dynamics are governed by Lindbladians, which introduce irreversible directions not captured by standard Lie algebras.
key_observables: The structure of the dynamical Lie wedge ($\mathcal{W}$), the total dissipation strength, and the classification into four structural types.
important_parameters: The dissipation strength, the structure of the solvable radical, and the coupling between semisimple and solvable parts.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the standard Lie algebra approach fails due to dissipation, necessitating the use of the Lie Wedge framework, which is constrained by physical requirements like Complete Positivity.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the structure implies diagrams illustrating the decomposition of the wedge into its semisimple and solvable components.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the known Levi decomposition for closed systems to the necessity of the Lie Wedge for open systems, culminating in the proposed decomposition theorem for the wedge itself, and providing concrete examples of failure (violating CCP) and successful classification.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep mathematical structure for understanding how dissipation fundamentally alters the algebraic description of quantum evolution, offering tools for classifying open quantum control systems.
